# The Lantern Keeper

Mara had been Ivo's apprentice at the Greyhaven lighthouse for two years. She cleaned the glass, trimmed the wick, carried oil up the narrow stairs, and listened while Ivo explained why the harbour lantern had to be lit before the evening tide. Beyond the harbour mouth lay Black Tooth Reef. In clear weather sailors could see it. In fog or storm, they trusted the lantern.

Mara wanted to become a licensed lantern keeper. She cared about earning Ivo's trust, but the work mattered to her for a simpler reason too: people at sea depended on it.

One autumn evening a storm came in faster than expected. While Ivo was securing a shutter, a gust threw him against the wall and badly twisted his ankle. He could not climb the tower stairs. The lantern was still dark, and the trading ship Gull Star was due before nightfall.

Before Mara could fetch the oil, Magistrate Rusk arrived. Rusk signed the papers that allowed apprentices to qualify for harbour work. He also owned warehouses on the quay. A ship belonging to one of his business rivals was carrying valuable cloth aboard the Gull Star.

"Leave the lantern dark for ten minutes," Rusk told Mara. "The Gull Star will turn back and miss the tide. My own ship will get the first berth."

Mara refused.

Rusk lowered his voice. "I decide whether your apprenticeship papers are accepted. Do as I say, or you may never work this harbour."

Mara was frightened. Losing her apprenticeship would mean losing two years of work and the future she had planned. But she also pictured the Gull Star approaching Black Tooth Reef in rain and darkness. Rusk's demand did not change what the lantern was for.

Ivo could not climb, but he could still tell Mara where the spare oil had been stored. Mara took the can, climbed the tower alone, cleaned rainwater from the lantern housing, filled the reservoir, and struck the flame. The lantern shone across the harbour just as the Gull Star appeared through the storm.

The captain saw the light, corrected the ship's course, and passed safely inside Black Tooth Reef.

When Mara came down, she told Ivo exactly what Rusk had said. Ivo reported the threat to the harbour council. Other workers described similar pressure from Rusk, and the council removed his authority over apprenticeship papers while it investigated him.

Mara did not become a keeper overnight, and no one gave her a prize. She remained Ivo's apprentice. The next evening, when it was time to prepare the lantern again, Ivo handed her the oil can without needing to remind her why the light mattered.
